title: Sex, Gender, and the Blogosphere: Looking Back at the Feminist Law Professors Blog, 2006-2024
affiliations: Pace University - School of Law

detail.title: Sex, Gender, and the Blogosphere: Looking Back at the Feminist Law Professors Blog, 2006-2024
detail.abstract: For eighteen years, the Feminist Law Professors blog served as a feminist-identified space for legal academics to collaborate, critique, and build community. This essay examines the blog's content, influence, and style; considers the pressures of sustaining a public feminist platform in legal academia; and evaluates its recognition as scholarly labor, with attention to citation practices, archiving, and institutional value. In situating the blog's legacy in a broader shift toward monetized and individualized digital media, the essay argues for the enduring need for collective feminist scholarly spaces, especially in times of political retrenchment and hostility to gender equity.

title: The Hidden Tax Game
affiliations: University of Akron - The George W. Daverio School of Accountancy

detail.title: The Hidden Tax Game
detail.abstract:
Taxation is not just a legal duty; it is a game, and the best players always win. While governments rely on laws and penalties to enforce compliance, corporations, high-net-worth individuals, and elite tax strategists exploit loopholes, turning complexity into opportunity. This Article argues that tax avoidance is not a flaw in the system, but an expected outcome. Modern tax law does not just permit avoidance; it actively encourages it. The more intricate the rules, the more valuable it becomes to manipulate them.

Using game theory as an analytical lens, this Article reframes taxation as a high-stakes competition, where strategic players respond to incentives, enforcement gaps, and shifting regulatory landscapes. Avoidance is not an anomaly but a rational reaction to the system's design. Governments, rather than serving as neutral enforcers, often reinforce the cycle with reactive policies that merely push tax planners toward new strategies. Those with the resources to navigate the system benefit, while ordinary taxpayers bear the burden.

Instead of increasing enforcement or making minor adjustments, this Article argues for a fundamental restructuring of tax law to change the rules of the game. By eliminating the conditions that make avoidance the smartest move through tax simplification, real-time taxation, and alternative revenue models, governments can realign incentives so that compliance becomes the optimal strategy. This approach shifts the focus from punishment to systemic reform, offering a new perspective on tax policy that targets avoidance at its root.

title: Analysis of Employment and Unemployment Rates in the Northwestern Federal District: Problems and Development Prospects (Анализ занятости населения и уровня безработицы в Северо-Западном федеральном округе: проблемы и перспективы развития)

detail.title: Analysis of Employment and Unemployment Rates in the Northwestern Federal District: Problems and Development Prospects (Анализ занятости населения и уровня безработицы в Северо-Западном федеральном округе: проблемы и перспективы развития)

publicationDetails.detailsText: Economics: Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow. 2024, Vol. 14, Is. 12A

detail.abstract:
English abstract: The article analyzes employment rates and the dynamics of unemployment in the Northwestern Federal District. The aim of the study was to identify the features of the dynamics of these indicators and to develop recommendations for the socio-economic development of the region's territories. A comparative analysis of employment and unemployment rates in the Russian Federation and the regions of the Northwestern Federal District was conducted, highlighting key regions such as Saint Petersburg, Leningrad Oblast, and the Nenets Autonomous Okrug, which lead in terms of the number of employed people. The authors formulate proposals for improving socio-economic development programs aimed at the development and exploration of the federal district's territories. Special attention is paid to the development of special programs that facilitate the relocation of state and commercial organizations to remote areas. In conclusion, it is noted that there is a need to organize infrastructure for the development of new territories, including the active involvement of private investments in the form of public-private partnerships. This contributes to the formation of a new economic environment and reduces the burden on federal cities.

Russian abstract: В статье анализируются показатели занятости населения и динамика уровня безработицы в Северо-Западном федеральном округе. Цель исследования заключалась в выявлении особенностей динамики этих показателей и разработке рекомендаций по социально-экономическому развитию территорий региона. Проведен сравнительный анализ показателей занятости и безработицы в Российской Федерации и регионах Северо-Западного федерального округа, выделены ключевые регионы, такие как Санкт-Петербург, Ленинградская область и Ненецкий автономный округ, которые лидируют по численности занятого населения. Авторы формулируют предложения по совершенствованию программ социально-экономического развития, направленных на освоение и развитие территорий федерального округа. Особое внимание уделено разработке специальных программ, способствующих перемещению государственных и коммерческих организаций в отдаленные районы. В заключении сделан вывод о необходимости организации инфраструктуры для развития новых территорий, включая активное привлечение частных инвестиций в форме государственно-частного партнерства. Это способствует формированию новой среды хозяйствования и снижению нагрузки на города федерального значения.

reference: Oxford Intersections: AI in Society, Forthcoming; doi.org/10.1093/9780198945215.003.0077.
title: Making AI Inevitable: Historical Perspective and the Problems of Predicting Long-Term Technological Change
affiliations: Georgetown University - Georgetown College and Georgetown University - Department of Government

detail.title: Making AI Inevitable: Historical Perspective and the Problems of Predicting Long-Term Technological Change

publicationDetails.detailsText: Oxford Intersections: AI in Society, Forthcoming; doi.org/10.1093/9780198945215.003.0077.

detail.abstract: This study demonstrates the extent to which prominent debates about the future of AI are best understood as subjective, philosophical disagreements over the history and future of technological change rather than as objective, material disagreements over the technologies themselves. It focuses on the deep disagreements over whether artificial general intelligence (AGI) will prove transformative for human society; a question that is analytically prior to that of whether this transformative effect will help or harm humanity. The study begins by distinguishing two fundamental camps in this debate. The first of these can be identified as "transformationalists," who argue that continued AI development will inevitably have a profound effect on society. Opposed to them are "skeptics," a more eclectic group united by their disbelief that AI can or will live up to such high expectations. Each camp admits further "strong" and "weak" variants depending on their tolerance for epistemic risk. These stylized contrasts help to identify a set of fundamental questions that shape the camps' respective interpretations of the future of AI. Three questions in particular are focused on: the possibility of non-biological intelligence, the appropriate time frame of technological predictions, and the assumed trajectory of technological development. In highlighting these specific points of non-technical disagreement, this study demonstrates the wide range of different arguments used to justify either the transformationalist or skeptical position. At the same time, it highlights the strong argumentative burden of the transformationalist position, the way that belief in this position creates competitive pressures to achieve first-mover advantage, and the need to widen the concept of "expertise" in debates surrounding the future development of AI.

title: Reimagining and Reconciling Antitrust and Access to Justice in the Political Economy
affiliations: Stetson University - College of Law

detail.title: Reimagining and Reconciling Antitrust and Access to Justice in the Political Economy
detail.abstract:
The intersection of antitrust law and access to justice is most noticeable where concentrated control over legal information systems has created barriers that undermine both competitive markets and equitable access to the judicial system. While antitrust law traditionally focuses on market efficiency and consumer welfare, this narrow economic framework fails to address how information monopolies in the legal sector systematically exclude marginalized communities from accessing justice.

The tension between data-driven innovation and market concentration is particularly acute in the legal sector, where the accumulation and control of legal information directly impacts democratic participation and the rule of law. Current antitrust enforcement, constrained by the consumer welfare standard, rarely extends beyond basic economic analysis to consider broader social justice implications. This limitation represents a fundamental mismatch between antitrust theory and the realities of information-dependent democracy.

Through a political economy lens, this article demonstrates that barriers to legal information access are not market accidents but the predictable result of institutional arrangements that treat antitrust as a neutral, efficiency-maximizing toolbox while masking its distributive choices. The narrow focus on economic competition limits interventions that could foster innovative legal service models and expand access to justice for underserved communities.

Reconciling traditional antitrust goals with access to justice requires acknowledging the ideological tensions inherent in treating legal information as a commodity. Only by expanding antitrust analysis beyond consumer welfare to encompass broader democratic values can policymakers address the systematic exclusion of marginalized groups from legal representation and court access. This expanded framework would recognize that competition in legal information markets is not merely about efficiency but about preserving the foundational promise of "equal justice under law."

title: Inducing Innovation at the Edge: Adding Marginal Complementors to a Mature Platform
affiliations: Northeastern University (USA)

detail.title: Inducing Innovation at the Edge: Adding Marginal Complementors to a Mature Platform
detail.abstract: Once a digital platform reaches maturity, attracting new complementors may affect innovation outcomes in ways that differ fundamentally from early-stage growth. We examine how inducement strategies to expand the complementor base of a mature platform shape incentives and motivations both to join and to engage in complementary development. Using data from the Apple App Store covering 501 long-tailed product markets, we compare three inducement types-monetary, nonmonetary (task-related intrinsic motivation), and cost-reducing-leveraging predetermined structural variation across markets to estimate causal effects. All three roughly double the installed base, with most additional complementors concentrated at the extreme end of the long tail of demand. Yet postentry development behaviors and innovation outcomes diverge sharply: non-monetary inducements spur more effort, iteration, and differentiated development; monetary inducements yield narrower, more commercially oriented outputs; and cost-based inducements produce lower discretionary development effort and greater redundancy. Cost-based inducements also significantly reduce the consumption-weighted quality of complements (in aggregate, not just within the long tail) relative to non-monetary inducements. These findings demonstrate that inducement strategies are not interchangeable: while all increase participation, their effects on innovation quality and diversity differ substantially, with important implications for platform governance in mature ecosystems.

title: A Cloud-to-Ground Lightning Prediction System for the Peruvian Andean Region Based on LSTM Networks and Electric Field Data
affiliations: Universidad Técnica Federico Santa María, Universidad Tecnica Federico Santa Maria and Pontificia Universidad Catolica de Valparaíso

detail.title: A Cloud-to-Ground Lightning Prediction System for the Peruvian Andean Region Based on LSTM Networks and Electric Field Data
detail.abstract: Cloud-to-ground lightning is among the most unpredictable and hazardous meteorological phenomena, posing significant risks to energy infrastructure and public safety. This study introduces a predictive system that leverages Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks trained with meteorological and environmental data collected in the Andean region of Peru. The model uses a memory-efficient data generator to handle multivariate time series and forecasts lightning occurrences at various lead times: 1, 5, 10, 15, and 24 hours. Input variables include temperature, relative humidity, atmospheric pressure, wind components, radiation, and ambient electric field measurements. Ground-truth lightning events are identified using data from the Geostationary Lightning Mapper (GLM) and the LINET detection system. Evaluation using the F1-score metric indicates strong performance, particularly for short-term horizons. The proposed approach provides a practical and scalable offline tool for lightning risk management in regions with limited real-time monitoring capabilities, supporting the development of early warning systems.

title: Analysis of Dow Jones Performance Around the Covid-19 Pandemic

detail.title: Analysis of Dow Jones Performance Around the Covid-19 Pandemic
detail.abstract: I investigate the hypothesis that large well-established publicly traded companies were price gouging after the COVID-19 pandemic. I calculate operating performance before, during, and after the pandemic for Dow Jones Industrial Average constituents. I present evidence that these companies did not price gouge consumers after the pandemic.

reference: Transactions: The Tennessee Journal of Business Law | Vol. 26 | 2025
title: NILs on Blockchains: The Good, The Bad, And Avoiding The Ugly
affiliations: University of Tennessee, Knoxville - Winston College of Law

detail.title: NILs on Blockchains: The Good, The Bad, And Avoiding The Ugly

publicationDetails.detailsText: Transactions: The Tennessee Journal of Business Law | Vol. 26 | 2025

detail.abstract:
The National Collegiate Athletic Association (the "NCAA") and colleges and universities have long benefitted financially from the name, image, and likeness (commonly known as "NIL") of student-athletes. Yet, until recently, collegiate athletes were not permitted to generate revenue from their NILs. Now, a collegiate athlete can benefit financially from their personal brand--their right of publicity--through arrangements in which others are granted rights to use their NILs.

Technological innovation facilitates the utilization of collegiate athlete branding. The Internet and its enablement of social media and digital advertising provide but one type of example. A less obvious digital technology that is facilitating NIL arrangements, however, is blockchain technology.

This article undertakes to begin an exploration of the potential advantages and disadvantages of NIL arrangements executed on blockchains primarily as a means of ascertaining and evaluating related legal and lawyering issues. In general, the article views these advantages from the perspective of the collegiate athlete and those who may represent them in NIL advice, compliance, and transactions, although it also includes certain information and reflections on relative values to other market participants (including the NCAA and colleges). To engage with this topic, the article first describes NIL arrangements generally and as they may relate to blockchain technologies. After establishing this foundational information, the article proceeds to isolate the positive and negative aspects of blockchain NIL arrangements and make related observations before offering a summary conclusion.

title: Optimizing the Development of Clinical Environments: An Integrative Review of Advanced Construction Management, Specialized Systems, and Patient-Centered Methodologies
affiliations: Institute for Advanced Construction and Smart Infrastructure Solutions of America

detail.title: Optimizing the Development of Clinical Environments: An Integrative Review of Advanced Construction Management, Specialized Systems, and Patient-Centered Methodologies

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. No personal or financial relationships with individuals or organizations were identified that could have influenced the content or findings of this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants or patient data; therefore, ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Construction management plays a vital role in healthcare facility development, presenting unique challenges and requirements that distinguish it from standard commercial construction. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on healthcare construction management practices, highlighting critical considerations for creating safe, efficient, and patient-centered environments. Healthcare construction demands specialized approaches to infection control, particularly regarding airborne and waterborne pathogens, necessitating rigorous implementation of Infection Control Risk Assessments and comprehensive Water Management Programs throughout all project phases. Unlike conventional construction, healthcare projects must often maintain operational continuity during renovations, requiring meticulous planning and execution to minimize disruptions to patient care while maintaining sterile environments. The integration of evidence-based design principles, advanced technologies including Building Information Modeling, and lean construction methodologies offers promising approaches for enhancing project efficiency and outcomes. Special consideration must be given to specialized systems including radiological shielding, medical gas installations, and complex MEP systems, requiring expertise that bridges both clinical requirements and technical specifications. The financial implications extend beyond traditional metrics to incorporate long-term operational costs, facility adaptability, and clinical outcomes-particularly significant given the aging infrastructure in many healthcare systems worldwide. By implementing comprehensive strategies that balance infection control, patient safety, operational efficiency, and long-term sustainability, healthcare facilities can create environments that support high-quality care delivery while adapting to evolving healthcare models and technological advancements.

title: The Last Mile to First Treatment: Search for Opioid Use Disorder Medication
affiliations: University of Arizona - Eller College of Management

detail.title: The Last Mile to First Treatment: Search for Opioid Use Disorder Medication
detail.abstract: Despite growing policy support for buprenorphine, the leading medication for opioid use disorder, treatment initiation remains low. Administrative insurance data from Washington State show only half of first-time patients fill their buprenorphine prescriptions, well below rates for other chronic conditions. I find initiation is hindered by limited availability and patients' inability to verify it beforehand. To quantify their impact, I develop a structural sequential search model in which patients are uncertain which pharmacies carry buprenorphine. Using purchase data alone, the model recovers search costs by assuming patients always visit their default (most frequently visited) pharmacy. This implies latent utility from the default depends only on preferences, while that from non-defaults reflects both preferences and search costs. I find fewer than 40% of patients search more than once. Counterfactual analysis shows that providing prescribers with real-time pharmacy inventory-to inform patients at the point of care-would increase buprenorphine initiation by approximately 17%.

title: Pricing, Delivery Time, and Greenness Decisions in Presence of Strategic Consumers: How Dynamic Delivery Time Can Improve the Profitability of the Supply Chain?
affiliations: University of Tehran, University of Tehran and University of North Carolina (UNC) at Charlotte - Business Information Systems and Operations Management Department

detail.title: Pricing, Delivery Time, and Greenness Decisions in Presence of Strategic Consumers: How Dynamic Delivery Time Can Improve the Profitability of the Supply Chain?
detail.abstract: Joint consideration of consumers’ strategic behavior and their sensitivity to delivery time, carbon emission, and price is an important problem which has been under-researched.  This study investigates a green supply chain with a manufacturer and an online retailer. Consumers are assumed to be sensitive to delivery time, carbon emission, price, and to behave strategically. We develop models with the objective of determining the optimal retail price, wholesale price, carbon emission reduction, and delivery time decisions in a manufacturer-retailer supply chain. In the first model, the retail price is determined dynamically, however, the delivery time is fixed throughout the selling season, whereas, in the second model, both the retail price and delivery time are quoted dynamically.  The results show that when consumers have relatively high sensitivity to the delivery time and are less strategic, dynamic delivery time quotation can increase the retailer’s profit. However, dynamic delivery time always increases the manufacturer’s profit. To better coordinate the supply chain we propose a cost-sharing contract that can improve the profitability of the supply chain. We further analyze the cost-sharing contract and present managerial insights into when it is profitable for both firms to enter into the contract.

title: Digitalization and Tokenization of Money: Exploring Central Bank Digital Currency Theories and Retail CBDC Developments in China
affiliations: The University of Hong Kong - Faculty of Law

detail.title: Digitalization and Tokenization of Money: Exploring Central Bank Digital Currency Theories and Retail CBDC Developments in China
detail.abstract: Central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) promote financial stability, inclusion and innovation in the digital economy. This article explores and reconceptualizes business management theories to enhance the understanding and characterization of CBDCs. From a theoretical standpoint, the governance, design principles and implementation of CBDCs align with institutional theory, stakeholder theory, technological innovation theory and open innovation theory. The interplay of these theories contributes to a comprehensive understanding of the interactions between CBDC stakeholders and the extensive array of opportunities and challenges presented by CBDCs. The theoretical frameworks are complemented by an examination of central banking legislation and monetary policy, as well as the potential impact on banking law and payment system regulations due to CBDC implementation, considering the significance of existing payment operators in facilitating CBDC distribution. In affording sufficient protection and in the interests of CBDC users, relevant issues in property law, data protection and privacy law are also considered. This article focuses on retail CBDCs, specifically China’s digital currency (e-CNY). As China’s central bank intends to cooperate with the G20 and other international organizations, e-CNY’s cross-border payments could have implications for monetary sovereignty, foreign exchange policies and regulatory compliance. China’s early e-CNY adoption serves as a vital case study for global central banks: CBDCs will likely have regulatory standards that reflect existing financial infrastructures and the ongoing US-China currency competition. This article aims to enhance understanding of legal challenges and practical concerns related to retail CBDCs, covering e-CNY’s core design features, CBDC’s impacts on existing laws, potential regulatory conflicts and competitiveness with existing payment systems. The article posits that account-based CBDCs can be considered a form of book money and can conform to the existing legal framework. Conversely, incorporating CBDCs into the present payment system necessitates recognizing token-based CBDCs as official payment methods, potentially requiring adjustments to pertinent legislation.

title: Robustness of Graph Embedding Methods for Community Detection
affiliations: Government of the United States of America - Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, Government of the United States of America - Oak Ridge National Laboratory and Government of the United States of America - Oak Ridge National Laboratory

detail.title: Robustness of Graph Embedding Methods for Community Detection
detail.abstract: This study investigates the robustness of graph embedding methods for community detection in the face of network perturbations, specifically edge deletions. Graph embedding techniques, which represent nodes as low-dimensional vectors, are widely used for various graph machine learning tasks due to their ability to capture structural properties of networks effectively. However, the impact of perturbations on the performance of these methods remains relatively understudied. The research considers state-of-the-art graph embedding methods from two families: matrix factorization (e.g., LE, LLE, HOPE, M-NMF) and random walk-based (e.g., DeepWalk, LINE, node2vec). Through experiments conducted on both synthetic and real-world networks, the study reveals varying degrees of robustness within each family of graph embedding methods. The robustness is found to be influenced by factors such as network size, initial community partition strength, and the type of perturbation. Notably, node2vec and LLE consistently demonstrate higher robustness for community detection across different scenarios, including networks with degree and community size heterogeneity. These findings highlight the importance of selecting an appropriate graph embedding method based on the specific characteristics of the network and the task at hand, particularly in scenarios where robustness to perturbations is crucial.

title: Law Proofing the Future
affiliations: University of Nebraska at Lincoln - College of Law

detail.title: Law Proofing the Future
detail.abstract:
Lawmakers today face continuous calls to "future proof" the legal system against generative artificial intelligence, algorithmic decision-making, targeted advertising, and all manner of emerging technologies. This Article takes a contrarian stance: It is not the law that needs bolstering for the future, but the future that needs protection from the law. From the printing press and the elevator to ChatGPT and online deepfakes, the recurring historical pattern is familiar. Technological breakthroughs provoke wonder, then fear, then legislation. The resulting legal regimes entrench incumbents, suppress experimentation, and displace long-standing legal principles with bespoke but brittle rules. Drawing from history, economics, political science, and legal theory, this Article argues that the most powerful tools for governing technological change the general-purpose tools of the common law-are in fact already on the books, long predating the technologies they are now called upon to govern, and ready also for whatever the future holds in store.

Rather than proposing any new statute or regulatory initiative, this Article offers something far rarer, a defense of doing less. It shows how the law's virtues-generality, stability, and adaptability-are best preserved not through prophylactic regulation, but through accretional judicial decision-making. The epistemic limits that make technological forecasting so unreliable and the hidden costs of early legislative intervention, including biased governmental enforcement and regulatory capture, mean that however fast technology may move, the law must not chase it. The case for legal restraint is thus not a defense of the status quo, but a call to reserve the conditions of freedom and equal justice under which both law and technology can evolve.

title: Ai in Strategic Leadership: Ethical Challenges and ESG Implications in the E-Retail Sector
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Ai in Strategic Leadership: Ethical Challenges and ESG Implications in the E-Retail Sector

keywords: E-retail sector and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA)

detail.abstract: This study explores the ethical challenges that emerge from the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into strategic leadership, with a particular emphasis on their implications for Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance in the e-retail sector. Adopting a mixed-methods approach, the research begins with a systematic literature review to establish the theoretical foundation and identify ethical concerns at the intersection of AI and leadership. This is followed by a confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) based on data collected from professionals in e-retail business environments to validate the identified challenges and assess their relative influence. The findings reveal a multifaceted landscape of ethical concerns, with algorithmic and technological factors exerting the strongest impact on leadership decision-making, while issues related to regulatory harmonisation and global governance appear less immediate in their effects. Importantly, several challenges—including data privacy, workforce equity, and algorithmic fairness—are shown to be directly linked to ESG dimensions, reinforcing the strategic value of ethical AI practices for responsible and sustainable organisational leadership. By offering empirically grounded insights, the study advances scholarly understanding of AI-enabled leadership and contributes to the broader discourse on e-commerce and ESG. It provides actionable implications for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers, highlighting the necessity of a comprehensive and collaborative approach to ensure that AI adoption in e-retail supports both business performance and societal responsibility.

title: Sustainable Consumption and Digital Influence: How Chinese Social Media Platforms Shape E-Commerce Behavior in Thailand
affiliations: Walailak University, Walailak University, Walailak University and Shandong Technology and Business University

detail.title: Sustainable Consumption and Digital Influence: How Chinese Social Media Platforms Shape E-Commerce Behavior in Thailand
detail.abstract: This research investigates the effect of Chinese social media platforms—WeChat, TikTok, and Xiaohongshu—on the sustainable buying practices of Thai young adults participating in cross-border e-commerce. By conducting 36 in-depth semi-structured interviews among 18- to 34-year-old respondents, the study explores the role of platform-level characteristics and algorithmic content on perceptions and practices towards sustainability. Results indicate that although the platforms raise awareness by featuring live-streaming purchase, peer ratings, and celebrity endorsements, the awareness does not constantly result in action. There were three consumer groups identified—Eco-Driven Idealists, Pragmatic Navigators, and Disengaged Bystanders—that had varied levels of motivation, trust, and behavioral intention.Despite the platforms’ potential to promote sustainability, challenges such as language barriers, unfamiliar platform ecosystems, and limited product transparency hinder deeper engagement. By applying the Theory of Planned Behavior and Value-Belief-Norm Theory, the study critically analyzes how attitudes, perceived norms, values, and accessibility issues shape sustainable consumption choices. The findings highlight both the transformative potential and structural limitations of Chinese platforms in influencing cross-cultural consumer behavior.This study urges companies to develop more inclusive, accessible, and culturally responsive marketing practices, and policymakers to enact regulatory policies decreasing greenwashing and increasing usability. Further research needs to advance on emotional and algorithmic effects, engage longitudinal research, and study platform effects on wider socio-cultural levels.

title: Immersive E-Commerce Interfaces: Evaluating Customer Experience in a Gesture-Controlled Digital Catalog
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and UCLouvain - Louvain Research Institute in Management and Organizations (LouRIM)

detail.title: Immersive E-Commerce Interfaces: Evaluating Customer Experience in a Gesture-Controlled Digital Catalog

keywords.keywords: Customer experienceElectroencephalographyGestural interactionDigital catalogE-commerceImmersive technologiesMachine learning

detail.abstract: As digital commerce evolves beyond basic functionality into immersive and emotionally engaging experiences, gestural interaction technologies offer promising avenues for transforming online customer journeys. Yet, their concrete impact on customer experience remains underexplored, particularly in ecologically valid commercial environments. This study examines how a gesture-controlled digital catalog, closely replicating a real e-commerce interface, influences cognitive, emotional, and behavioral responses compared to a traditional mouse-based interface.Using a within-subject experimental design, we combine self-reported questionnaires with electroencephalographic (EEG) data and machine learning analysis to capture both subjective impressions and objective neural responses. Our results show that gestural interaction significantly enhances playfulness, immersion, and emotional arousal, while also increasing cognitive load and memorization effort. However, it reduces perceived control, particularly among older users, highlighting the need for adaptive onboarding strategies. By demonstrating the experiential benefits of gesture-controlled interfaces, this study contributes to the ongoing digital transformation of e-commerce, where intuitive and embodied interactions redefine the customer journey. Our findings contribute to the e-commerce literature by demonstrating how next-generation interaction technologies can reshape the customer experience. We also illustrate the added value of AI-driven neuroanalytics for uncovering hidden patterns in customer experience data. For practitioners, we provide actionable insights for designing intuitive, inclusive, and emotionally engaging customer journeys using next-generation interaction technologies.

title: A Systematic Review of E-Commerce Digital Transformation: Insights into the Paradigm Shift Towards a Human-Centric Industrial Revolution
affiliations: Robert Gordon University, Robert Gordon University, Robert Gordon University and Robert Gordon University

detail.title: A Systematic Review of E-Commerce Digital Transformation: Insights into the Paradigm Shift Towards a Human-Centric Industrial Revolution
detail.abstract: BackgroundThis systematic literature review examines the evolution of digital transformation in e-commerce from 2017 to 2024, with a focus on the intersection of technology, organisational priorities, and human-centric insights aligned with Industry 5.0. The review addresses two key questions: (1) What are the key characteristics and trajectory of research on e-commerce digital transformation? and (2) How have the technological, organisational, and human-centric themes evolved over time?MethodWe searched Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore for articles published up to June 30, 2024. Screening was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines, using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. A total of 119 studies were included after a four-stage screening process. Descriptive statistics and thematic synthesis were used for data analysis.ResultsThe results show a steady growth trend on the topic, with 119 studies published across 55 countries and 96 journals, with China as the main contributor. Research evolved through three phases: Early Years (2017–2019): the foundational exploration era, Increased Momentum (2020–2021): strategic adaptation era, and Growth (2022–2023): resilience, personalisation, and sustainability era.ConclusionKey technologies identified include AI, big data, CRM, blockchain, and IoT, with increasing emphasis on ethical and human-centric innovation. Findings highlight a paradigm shift toward human-centric digital transformation, predicated on the ethical use of technology, agile leadership, and data-driven personalisation. Limitations include excluding conference papers and restricted access to some full texts of relevant articles.

title: A Study of Collaborative Robot Adoption by Korea's Small and Medium-Sized Manufacturers
affiliations: Georgia Institute of Technology, Georgia Institute of Technology and Georgia Institute of Technology

detail.title: A Study of Collaborative Robot Adoption by Korea's Small and Medium-Sized Manufacturers
detail.abstract: This study investigates the factors influencing the adoption of collaborative robots (cobots) by small and medium-sized manufactures (SMMs) in South Korea, employing the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework combined with Innovation Ecosystem theory. Through in-depth interviews with industry experts, the research identifies critical technological factors such as functionality, cost, and perceived benefits and highlights that limited performance and higher initial costs can hinder adoption. Organizational factors, including a firm’s technical capabilities, prior robot experience, and worker upskilling, significantly shape adoption decisions, often necessitating support from external intermediaries. Environmental factors, notably government policy programs, domestic suppliers, and integrators substantially facilitate adoption by reducing financial and operational barriers, enhancing trialability, and fostering collaboration within an innovation ecosystem. Broader socio-economic conditions, such as rising labor costs, workforce aging, and labor shortages exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, further accelerate cobot adoption as essential for survival rather than merely cost reduction. The research concludes that a comprehensive approach integrating both internal firm capabilities and external ecosystem support is crucial for successful adoption.

title: Business on the Ballot: Employee Voting as Nonmarket Strategy
affiliations: Columbia University - Columbia Business School, Management

detail.title: Business on the Ballot: Employee Voting as Nonmarket Strategy
detail.abstract: Can employees help firms complete in the nonmarket arena? Research on nonmarket strategy has recognized constituency building as a form of corporate political activity (CPA), but there has been limited investigation into whether and how firms can rely upon employees to support their political goals. While employees would seem a promising target for constituency building, research suggests that employees often react negatively when firms communicate political messages, making it unclear if firms can or should rely upon employees to support CPA. I develop and test a theory that firms can rely on employees' political support when two conditions are met: first, that the policy issue is non-partisan, and second, that there are clear strategic implications for the firm and its employees. To test this theory, I look at an important but understudied political context: direct democracy via non-partisan ballot questions at the U.S. state and local level. Using an unprecedented dataset which links millions of U.S. workers with their election turnout records, I employ difference-indifferences and find that employees and members of their households turn out to vote at significantly higher rates versus unaffected voters in low-turnout elections featuring ballot questions with strategic implications for their employer (up to 33 p.p. for employees and up to 13 p.p. for household members). These findings present novel theoretical insights and empirical evidence about how firms can influence policy outcomes and speak to broader questions about firms' impact on society.

title: Optimizing Podiatry Appointments to Improve Efficiency, Prevent Wastage and Save Costs by Leveraging Electronic Health Record Functionality at a Tertiary Care Hospital Network in Singapore
affiliations: National University of Singapore (NUS) - Ng Teng Fong General Hospital, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, National University of Singapore (NUS) - Ng Teng Fong General Hospital and National University of Singapore (NUS) - Ng Teng Fong General Hospital

detail.title: Optimizing Podiatry Appointments to Improve Efficiency, Prevent Wastage and Save Costs by Leveraging Electronic Health Record Functionality at a Tertiary Care Hospital Network in Singapore
detail.abstract: IntroductionHigh-risk diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) patients require timely podiatry care to prevent complications, but clinic delays from high demand and full schedules pose challenges. Missed appointments, which may be predictable, present an opportunity to reallocate slots to urgent cases. Leveraging electronic health record (EHR) systems can optimize this process, reducing manual effort and improving access for high-risk patients.  MethodsWe used Lean Six Sigma (LSS) ‘Plan-Do-Check-Act’ approach to identify opportunities to improve early access to podiatry services for high-risk DFU patients. A reporting tool, Reporting Work Bench® (RWB®), within Epic® EHR was used to identify and reallocate future out-patient podiatry slots taken up by patients admitted as inpatient in the acute care hospital.  ResultsA total of 97 such appointments were identified over one year (January to December 2023), constituting 10.77% (97/901) of total ‘no-show’ appointments. 52.6% of these slots were utilized by high-risk patients needing urgent care (51/97 patients), 90% of these patients presented with active foot ulcers, and nearly 50% were classified as being at moderate or high risk for amputation within one year, based on the WIfI Classification System. Additionally, time saved to find one appointment was reduced from 5 minutes per slot to 1 minute translating to an estimated cost saving of SGD$ 3500 annually.  ConclusionOur study demonstrates successful implementation of LSS principles to optimize and enhance early access to podiatry services for high-risk DFU patients. Leveraging EHR functionality helped prioritise care of patients with high-risk DFUs while reducing wastage and improving operational efficiency.

title: Integrating Sustainability into the 7Ps of Pharmaceutical Marketing: A Conceptual Framework for Brand Building

detail.title: Integrating Sustainability into the 7Ps of Pharmaceutical Marketing: A Conceptual Framework for Brand Building

detail.abstract: Purpose This paper reimagines the strategic role of pharmaceutical marketing by extending the classical 7Ps framework to reflect contemporary priorities such as trust, sustainability, and stakeholder alignment. It introduces the 7Ps-3D model, which incorporates "Green P" (sustainability) as a central marketing lever and connects strategic inputs to brand-building outcomes that go beyond prescribing behavior. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review, following PRISMA guidelines, was conducted across 64 empirical studies published between 2013 and 2024. Key constructs were identified through bibliometric mapping (using Litmaps Pro) and qualitative thematic coding (via NVivo). These findings were further refined through insights gathered from senior pharmaceutical marketers. Findings The review uncovered three persistent gaps in existing literature: a predominant focus on promotional tactics, limited attention to downstream brand outcomes, and the near absence of sustainability-oriented marketing levers. The proposed 7Ps-3D framework addresses these gaps by linking seven strategic inputs-including the newly defined Green P-to three cascading brand outcomes: prescribing behavior (D1), brand loyalty and trust (D2), and stakeholder engagement (D3). Originality/value This is the first conceptual model to integrate sustainability into the 7Ps marketing mix and link it to measurable brand outcomes. It offers theoretical insight and practical relevance, especially for high-trust, regulated sectors like pharmaceuticals. Research limitations While grounded in literature and validated through expert discussions, the model remains conceptual. Empirical testing in healthcare settings is needed to confirm its applicability. Practical implications The framework equips pharmaceutical leaders with a structured tool to craft strategies that balance commercial performance and long-term reputational value.

title: Mandatory Human Rights Due Diligence Legislation: Embeddedness, Compliance, and Enforcement
affiliations: The Stephen M. Ross School of Business at the University of Michigan

detail.title: Mandatory Human Rights Due Diligence Legislation: Embeddedness, Compliance, and Enforcement

publicationDetails.detailsText: University of Pennsylvania Journal of Business Law, forthcoming

detail.abstract: Recent years have seen a significant shift in corporate accountability for human rights violations through the adoption of mandatory human rights due diligence (HRDD) legislation, particularly the European Union’s Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD). HRDD is the process by which corporations proactively identify negative human rights impacts connected to their supply chains and then implement corrective actions.  A key concern is that corporations may treat these legislative requirements as a superficial “tick-box” exercise, undermining their effectiveness. This Article argues that successful HRDD implementation requires embedding the process within the organization under the guidance of the compliance function. This does not mean that the compliance function should assume control of HRDD activities, but rather that HRDD governance should be integrated into the corporation’s existing compliance program. Under this approach, compliance provides oversight, ensures accountability, and fosters a corporate culture that respects human rights. By outlining the components of a modern compliance program—some of which challenge conventional perceptions of compliance—this Article illustrates how compliance can help embed respect for human rights into the organization’s culture. Additionally, this Article proposes enforcement strategies that regulators can adopt to incentivize deeper HRDD integration. A compliance-informed regulatory approach can enhance the effectiveness of HRDD laws, ensuring they work to prevent human rights violations rather than merely minimize corporate liability.
